s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of loss of consciousness, visual disturbances, and headaches with associated vertigo, dizziness, and postural weakness, suggesting a complex vascular and neurological presentation
salient_findings: Recurrent blackouts
Blurring of vision
Moderate frontal headaches radiating to the whole head
Vertigo, dizziness, palpitations, and postural weakness
Deficient pulses in both upper limbs
Bruit audible over the left subclavian fossa
Optic-disk cupping with irregular margins in the right eye
key_facts: Abnormal liver tests (direct bilirubin 0.3 mg/dL; ALT 152 U/L; ALP 317 U/L)
Computed tomography angiogram showing diffuse intimal thickening with narrowing at the origins of the brachiocephalic, right common carotid, and left subclavian arteries

shortlist.label: Takayasu arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse intimal thickening with narrowing at the origins of the brachiocephalic, right common carotid, and left subclavian arteries, and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Subclavian steal syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bruit audible over the left subclavian fossa and deficient pulses in both upper limbs

shortlist.label: Moyamoya disease
shortlist.why_kept: Optic-disk cupping with irregular margins and recurrent episodes of loss of consciousness

shortlist.label: Giant cell arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and abnormal liver tests

shortlist.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
shortlist.why_kept: Microcytosis, hypochromasia, and elevated serum ferritin, suggesting systemic vasculitis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including recurrent blackouts, vertigo, dizziness, and postural weakness, along with the presence of a bruit over the left subclavian fossa and deficient pulses in both upper limbs, are consistent with large vessel vasculitis. The computed tomography angiogram showing diffuse intimal thickening with narrowing at the origins of the brachiocephalic, right common carotid, and left subclavian arteries supports this diagnosis. Additionally, the patient's elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein levels indicate inflammation, which is a hallmark of Takayasu arteritis.

rejected.label: Subclavian steal syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has symptoms consistent with subclavian steal syndrome, such as vertigo and dizziness, the presence of systemic inflammation and involvement of multiple arteries suggests a more widespread process like Takayasu arteritis.

rejected.label: Moyamoya disease
rejected.why: Moyamoya disease typically presents with stroke or transient ischemic attack, and is characterized by narrowing of the internal carotid artery and its branches, which is not consistent with the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Giant cell arteritis
rejected.why: Giant cell arteritis typically affects older adults and is characterized by headache, jaw claudication, and visual symptoms, which are not prominent in this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
rejected.why: Polyarteritis nodosa typically affects medium-sized arteries and is characterized by systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, and abdominal pain, which are not present in this patient.
